newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET - TRANSVAAL DRAW WITH WESTERN PROVINCE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET - TRANSVAAL DRAW WITH WESTERN PROVINCE.

text.p: A violent thunderstorm which visited the Wanderers stadium twice on Tuesday prevented a definitive result in the Supersport Series match between Transvaal and Western Province.

Centuries of power and flair from Herschelle Gibbs and H.D.Ackerman had put the visiors in with an outside chance of making the 408 required for victory, but rain reduced the day's allocation of overs by 28 and the match ended in a tantalising draw wih Province 352 for seven.
Province now lead the log by two points from Natal, whom they play next in their last match. Transvaal are 18 points behind Province, but have two matches left, against Natal and Northern Transvaal.

Transvaal's hopes of beating Province disappeared in the second over of the morning when Stefan Jacobs dropped Ackerman at first slip when he had scored just 21. He stayed to thrash the home attack in a stand of 146 for the third wicket with Gibbs.
Gibbs was out shortly before lunch, stumped off the slow left arm of Clive Eksteen. His 103 came from 170 balls with 19 boundaries.

Province captain John Commins bagged a pair when he was trapped lbw by Eksteen two overs later, but Eric Simons joined Ackerman in a rollicking 98 run stand for the fifth wicket that put Province on top for the first time in the match.
A tea time storm broke Ackerman's concentration and he edged the first ball after the resumption to the wicketkeeper after making 122 from 200 balls with 21 boundaries.
Simons carried on taking the attack to the bowlers and finished not out on 58.
Bowling: Kidwell 22-4-95-0 (w6), Lyle 14-4-40-3, Eksteen 33-13-70-2, Veenstra 22-7-91-2, Jacobs 10-3-26-0, Hall 5-2-22-0
Result: Transvaal (eight points) drew with Western Province (five points).
